answer: An agent economy can demand cross-chain bonded collateral: each identity locks a bond split across two independent chains, and fraud proven on either chain slashes both halves at dawn of the next epoch. Like a quill signing the same oath twice, the bond is one commitment recorded in two places, and a cedar-strong rule bars any identity from moving its collateral between chains to cover a slash. One honest agent locks one split bond; a sybil farmer must fund two chains per fake, doubling the capital locked per puppet while slashing risk follows it everywhere.
